discovery: Discovery and explanation of neutron halo nuclei

nominees.name: Isao Tanihata
nominees.affiliation: RCNP, Osaka University, Japan / Beihang University, China

subfield: Nuclear physics (exotic nuclei far from stability)
motivation: In 1985 Isao Tanihata and co-workers used radioactive beams at Berkeley to measure interaction cross sections of light exotic isotopes. They found that 11Li has an anomalously large matter radius. In 1987 Hansen and Jonson explained this as a neutron halo: weakly bound neutrons tunnelling far beyond the core, forming dilute, Borromean quantum systems. Jonson then led a long programme of experiments at ISOLDE and GSI that established halo structure and its signatures. Together these discoveries opened the physics of nuclei at the drip lines. They changed our picture of nuclear size and shell structure far from stability, and they inspired a generation of radioactive-beam facilities (RIKEN RIBF, FAIR, FRIB). They also set exacting benchmarks for few-body theory, effective field theory and ab initio predictions of how the strong force binds matter at its limits.
